resources.string: The system turned off the mock location permission, so the game may see your real location. Go to Developer options and select this app again.

The system changed the \"Select mock location app\" setting. Go to Developer options → Select mock location app → choose \"Pikmin Bloom GPS\", or run adb shell appops set app.pikminbloom.gps android:mock_location allow from a computer. If the game has already seen your real location, the app stays on your real location and won\'t jump back by itself.

Google Maps is open, but the game and Maps both see the virtual location. Tap here to switch to real location (the game will jump once). If you\'re just looking up a shop or reading reviews, you can ignore this.

While it's on, Play services works out your real location on its own from nearby Wi-Fi and cell towers. If the mock slips even briefly, the game may see your real location (and jump back to where you really are). With it off, only GPS is left, and during a patrol the GPS is mocked by this app.

Where: Settings → Location → Location services → Google Location Accuracy (the name varies a little by phone maker).

Trade-off: when you're not patrolling, Maps and other apps locate you more slowly and less accurately indoors, and getting your real location when a patrol starts may take a few extra seconds (faster near a window).
The game saw your real location

The mock location failed and the game saw your real location (%1$s from the virtual location). To avoid jumping back and forth between the two, it switched to \"Real location\" and the virtual patrol waits where it was. To go back, open the app and tap \"Back to virtual location…\" (it jumps again).
The game saw your real location, so it stays on real location (won\'t jump back by itself). Tap the location button to go back
The mock location failed and the game saw your real location, so it switched to \"Real location\" to stop jumping back and forth. To go back, tap \"Back to virtual location…\"
